discovery.title: Confirm the source route
discovery.note: Run from the machine that will send the scan. Keep the assigned scope explicit.

findings.finding: A route selects the expected interface/source
findings.check: Reachability still needs a probe; a route lookup alone is not a live host.

fallback.reason: No response from host discovery: test the assigned host without assuming it is offline.

discovery.commands:
```bash
ip addr
ip route get TARGET
nmap -sn SUBNET -oA host-discovery
```

discovery.title: Build a TCP port list with Nmap
discovery.note: The command below scans all TCP ports with SYN privileges. Create the scans output directory first; use the complete connect-scan variant when unprivileged. Keep the fast initial pass distinct from full coverage.

findings.finding: An open TCP port
findings.check: Run focused service detection on the discovered ports, including nonstandard ones.

fallback.reason: Only TCP was checked: investigate UDP when the objective or DNS/SNMP/RPC clues call for it.

discovery.title: Identify the responding application
discovery.note: Keep the endpoint and raw service output; choose the matching client from its response.

findings.finding: SMB/RPC responds
findings.check: Check anonymous or known-identity share access.

findings.finding: An HTTP response or redirect
findings.check: Resolve the correct scheme and hostname before directory discovery.

findings.finding: An unrecognized listener
findings.check: Send a protocol-specific probe instead of choosing an exploit by port number.

fallback.reason: Results conflict with client behavior: rebuild the endpoint queue from confirmed responses.

discovery.commands:
```bash
nmap -Pn -sV -p PORTS TARGET -oA selected-services
nmap --script-help SCRIPT_NAME
```

services.title: Try SMB with the actual access context
services.note: Use the anonymous form first when no credentials exist; use the authenticated variant when an identity is available.

findings.finding: A readable share contains config, backups or keys
findings.check: Read the exact file and record its source before testing any recovered value.

findings.finding: A working domain identity
findings.check: Enumerate domain shares with that identity; share listing alone is not file access.

fallback.reason: SMB is denied: inspect another discovered protocol, not repeated guesses against the same identity.

services.title: Query exposed names and configuration
services.note: Use only an observed/assigned community and the correct SNMP version; preserve the returned OIDs.

findings.finding: Process arguments or configuration contain an account value
findings.check: Classify its account scope and format.

findings.finding: A hostname or directory-service clue
findings.check: Resolve it through the relevant name service.

fallback.reason: No useful SNMP response: return to the confirmed service list and choose its native client.

services.title: Inspect database identity and grants
services.note: Use this branch only for confirmed SQL Server with an accepted login. Other database clients are separate procedures.

findings.finding: A permitted impersonation or command facility
findings.check: Check the effective login and the exact enabled operation before attempting an OS effect.

findings.finding: MySQL/MariaDB identified instead of SQL Server
findings.check: Use the MySQL/MariaDB grants and file rules rather than SQL Server syntax.

fallback.reason: Login succeeds but the action is denied: inspect grants under the same identity.

web-mapping.title: Capture a real request before fuzzing
web-mapping.note: Use the browser/proxy to capture the real method, host, cookie and input; curl is the replay baseline.

findings.finding: Redirect to a different hostname
findings.check: Resolve and replay that hostname before testing paths.

findings.finding: A login, upload or object endpoint
findings.check: Capture its normal authenticated request and available roles.

fallback.reason: Every request reaches the wrong/default site: fix the host/scheme/session first.

web-mapping.commands:
```bash
curl -skD headers.txt -o body.html http://TARGET:PORT/
curl -skI https://TARGET:PORT/
```

web-mapping.title: Discover paths with Gobuster or the documented ffuf variant
web-mapping.note: First request a missing path to learn the false-positive body/status/length. Keep the correct host and session.

findings.finding: A backup, config, source or repository path
findings.check: Read its content; a 200 response alone does not establish an artifact.

findings.finding: A new application function
findings.check: Map its parameters and authorization boundary.

fallback.reason: All candidates look identical: repair the response controls rather than collecting more false positives.

web-mapping.title: Enumerate hostname-selected sites
web-mapping.note: Use this when DNS, certificates, redirects or page content suggest another hostname.

findings.finding: A host has a distinct response
findings.check: Browse it with the correct Host header and repeat function/path mapping.

fallback.reason: No distinct host: return to real application functions and exposed scripts.

web-exploitation.title: Test the primitive exposed by the real request
web-exploitation.note: Use this command branch only when an input reaches a utility/command context. Match the observed OS/parser.

findings.finding: Target UID/name appears only in the test response
findings.check: Verify the destination and process identity; then choose a viable session route.

findings.finding: Only a repeatable controlled delay is visible
findings.check: Use the blind verification variants; one slow request proves nothing.

fallback.reason: Input is only reflected: investigate another mapped input or mechanism.

web-exploitation.title: For file inputs, prove actual file read
web-exploitation.note: Keep session and request method intact; choose a target file appropriate to the observed platform.

findings.finding: Recognizable file contents
findings.check: Retrieve relevant application config/source; classify any recovered material.

findings.finding: A PHP include sink accepts a filter wrapper
findings.check: Test source disclosure separately from file execution.

fallback.reason: Only an error/template/status changed: return to request mapping; do not claim a file read.

web-exploitation.title: For uploads, locate the stored file and its handler
web-exploitation.note: Acceptance, storage, retrieval and server-side execution are separate tests.

findings.finding: A controlled file is stored and retrieved
findings.check: Check extension, interpreter and executable handler before choosing an execution payload.

findings.finding: The upload destination path is controllable
findings.check: Identify the consumer that will use that exact location.

fallback.reason: No compatible handler/consumer: treat it as storage and investigate another application boundary.

public-exploits.title: Find a PoC for the confirmed component
public-exploits.note: SearchSploit/advisory results are candidates. Read the feature, build, authentication and configuration requirements.

findings.finding: The vulnerable feature and required access match
findings.check: Read the PoC code and recreate its runtime before execution.

fallback.reason: Only the banner/version matches: return to component enumeration.

public-exploits.commands:
```bash
searchsploit --cve CVE
searchsploit -t "PRODUCT VERSION"
searchsploit PRODUCT VERSION --exclude="/dos/"
```

public-exploits.title: Inspect interpreter, dependencies and request assumptions
public-exploits.note: Do not debug blindly by changing payloads; separate a local runtime failure from a target-side rejection.

findings.finding: Native source/build mismatch
findings.check: Match process architecture and ABI before compiling.

findings.finding: Login, CSRF, path or schema differs
findings.check: Reconstruct the real protected request.

fallback.reason: The program runs but no effect is verified: return to the advisory's exact conditions.

sessions-transfers.title: Verify the host and command identity
sessions-transfers.note: A single response is not necessarily a stable session. Record the actual destination and output channel.

findings.finding: Commands execute as the expected target identity
findings.check: Choose the available callback direction and interpreter.

findings.finding: Callback cannot reach the listener
findings.check: Inspect the actual initiator, destination and route.

fallback.reason: Output cannot be attributed to the destination: repeat the host/identity proof.

sessions-transfers.commands:
```bash
hostname
id
pwd
ip addr
ip route
```

sessions-transfers.title: Transfer a reviewed tool through a reachable route
sessions-transfers.note: Serve from the attacker and download on the target only when that direction is reachable. Verify the received artifact.

findings.finding: The verified Linux enumerator is present
findings.check: Run the LinPEAS baseline and inspect its findings.

findings.finding: HTTP is unavailable but SSH file access works
findings.check: Use SCP instead of forcing the same failing transport.

findings.finding: SMB is the usable authenticated channel
findings.check: Use the SMB transfer procedure in that identity.

fallback.reason: Bytes differ or the file is missing: fix transfer before interpreting execution errors.

credentials.title: Identify the artifact before using a cracking tool
credentials.note: Keep provenance and local/domain/application account scope. Hash-looking text is not automatically an NT hash.

findings.finding: A plaintext password
findings.check: Test the matching identity on one relevant reachable service.

findings.finding: An SSH private key
findings.check: Check key format, protection and the intended account.

findings.finding: A ticket/cache
findings.check: Check principal, service scope, expiry and a compatible client.

fallback.reason: Format is still unknown: inspect the artifact before selecting a Hashcat/John mode.

credentials.title: Use Hashcat/John only after format identification
credentials.note: Select the documented format-specific mode and an offline candidate list; recovery is not proof of service access.

findings.finding: A password is recovered
findings.check: Validate the account scope and relevant service permission.

findings.finding: A reusable NT hash rather than a recoverable plaintext password
findings.check: Use only protocols and clients supporting that material.

fallback.reason: No recovery: revisit artifact type and feasible candidates; enumerate other evidence instead of assuming the account is unusable.

credentials.commands:
```bash
hashcat -a 0 -m MODE hashes.txt wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule --session job
hashcat -m MODE hashes.txt --show
```

linux-privesc.title: Identify the session, then run LinPEAS early
linux-privesc.note: After checking id, architecture and shell availability, transfer a trusted reviewed LinPEAS copy using the transfer procedure. The sh invocation does not need an executable bit. Save output; use the local -h before selecting optional flags.

findings.finding: sudo/NOPASSWD or an allowed binary
findings.check: Run sudo -l and compare run-as, exact path and permitted arguments with the chosen escape.

findings.finding: A root-owned SUID binary
findings.check: Check the exact file, mount flags and its available privileged operation.

findings.finding: A useful file capability
findings.check: Match the capability to the exact executable operation and mount.

findings.finding: A password, key or application config
findings.check: Read the source file and identify which account/service it belongs to.

fallback.reason: LinPEAS cannot run or shows no usable finding: use the native identity/permissions checks; quiet output does not prove no escalation.

linux-privesc.commands:
```bash
id
uname -m
command -v bash python3
ls -ld /tmp
```

```bash
sh ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt
```

linux-privesc.title: Check sudo rules against the actual binary
linux-privesc.note: Use only the operation permitted by the entire rule. Select the matching GTFOBins mode/build instead of trying every example.

findings.finding: (root) NOPASSWD permits a useful interpreter/helper
findings.check: Check argument restrictions and privilege retention, then use that exact permitted invocation.

findings.finding: LD_PRELOAD is explicitly permitted/preserved
findings.check: Verify a dynamically linked allowed program and the variable-setting permission.

fallback.reason: No useful sudo rule: check SUID/SGID and capabilities; do not keep trying sudo payloads.

linux-privesc.title: Catch short-lived root jobs with pspy
linux-privesc.note: Use a reviewed binary matching the target architecture; keep it running long enough to observe the suspected schedule. Stop after collecting the needed events.

findings.finding: UID=0 repeatedly invokes a script under /opt or another path
findings.check: Check the script and each parent with namei/stat/getfacl, then identify the schedule/trigger.

findings.finding: A privileged job invokes a helper without an absolute path
findings.check: Inspect the real PATH and a writable directory searched first.

fallback.reason: No event was observed: inspect cron/timers/services directly rather than assuming no privileged job exists.

linux-privesc.title: Test SUID/capability findings manually
linux-privesc.note: Use native discovery alongside the tool output; a flagged executable is only useful if it retains a relevant privilege.

findings.finding: A root-owned SUID program exposes a usable operation
findings.check: Check nosuid, exact build and effective identity after that operation.

findings.finding: An executable has a useful file capability
findings.check: Check the named capability and its effective operation under this mount.

findings.finding: A root-consumed file/parent is writable
findings.check: Validate the real consumer and trigger before modification.

fallback.reason: No useful privileged executable: return to secrets, scheduled consumers, mounts and local-only services.

windows-privesc.title: Record the token and host context
windows-privesc.note: Check the current token before choosing an exploit or collector build.

findings.finding: SeImpersonatePrivilege
findings.check: Check its enabled state and the operation/access needed by that specific technique.

findings.finding: SeBackupPrivilege
findings.check: Inspect the permitted backup operation and the exact source it can read.

findings.finding: Service/task activity or a useful group membership
findings.check: Inspect the actual objects and ACLs.

fallback.reason: No immediate token route: run the broad collector, then verify its service/file findings.

windows-privesc.title: Run winPEAS early and save its report
windows-privesc.note: Transfer a reviewed binary matching the host architecture. The log option writes out.txt; inspect it before selecting a route. Native checks remain available if execution is blocked.

findings.finding: Modifiable service or writable service binary
findings.check: Check sc qc/sdshow and the actual binary/parent ACL, service account and restart rights.

findings.finding: Unquoted service path
findings.check: Check the exact executable prefixes for write access and a privileged restartable consumer.

findings.finding: A saved credential/config finding
findings.check: Read the named source and classify the account/material.

fallback.reason: The collector is blocked or reports no useful candidate: continue native ACL/service/task inspection.

windows-privesc.title: Verify the specific service/task route
windows-privesc.note: Configuration write, binary replacement, unquoted-prefix write and dependency loading require different rights.

findings.finding: Service configuration can be changed
findings.check: Confirm the service runs as a stronger identity and you can cause a start/restart.

findings.finding: Only the binary or its parent is writable
findings.check: Check replacement semantics, the consumer identity and a trigger.

findings.finding: A scheduled task consumes a writable file
findings.check: Inspect the task principal, action and schedule.

fallback.reason: The highlighted path is not effectively writable: reject that candidate and inspect another actual object.

windows-privesc.commands:
```cmd
whoami /all
icacls "C:\Path\To\OBJECT"
icacls "C:\Path\To"
sc.exe sdshow SERVICE
```

ad-mapping.title: Resolve domain, DC, DNS and clock first
ad-mapping.note: Use the current domain identity or the supported query context; wrong naming/transport can look like a bad password.

findings.finding: Domain/DC preflight works
findings.check: Enumerate users/groups/SPNs and collect supported directory relationships.

fallback.reason: KDC timeout, name failure or skew: repair that dependency before judging credentials.

ad-mapping.title: Collect a BloodHound directory baseline with SharpHound
ad-mapping.note: Use a collector compatible with the BloodHound version. DCOnly is a directory baseline, not proof of all host/session edges.

findings.finding: A useful object-control edge
findings.check: Resolve the controlled trustee, target object and effective ACE.

findings.finding: A host/session edge
findings.check: Check destination rights and session freshness independently.

findings.finding: An account with an SPN
findings.check: Check the actual account/SPN and ticket-request conditions.

fallback.reason: Collection is blocked or incomplete: query the relevant objects manually.

ad-identities.title: Inspect the tickets/material already available
ad-identities.note: Use the current identity and ticket cache before attempting credential collection or ticket construction.

findings.finding: A valid service-scoped ticket
findings.check: Check service principal, expiry and the matching client.

findings.finding: A privileged local token and an accessible credential source
findings.check: Check protection and exact source prerequisites before selecting a collector.

fallback.reason: No useful ticket/source: inspect account configuration and object rights with the available domain identity.

ad-identities.title: Choose AS-REP or SPN roasting from account evidence
ad-identities.note: Use this branch only for a confirmed preauthentication-disabled account; ordinary SPN accounts use a different request.

findings.finding: A valid AS-REP response for the known account
findings.check: Use the type-specific offline recovery path.

findings.finding: A normal service account with an SPN
findings.check: Request the matching service ticket in an authenticated context.

fallback.reason: The account requires preauthentication: stop this path and inspect SPNs or effective object rights.

ad-identities.title: Resolve an ACL edge to its concrete operation
ad-identities.note: Use the exact trustee, target class, GUID and inheritance/deny behavior, not the graph label alone.

findings.finding: Effective password-reset right on the intended user
findings.check: Confirm account state and the effect of changing its password.

findings.finding: Effective write to a useful group's member attribute
findings.check: Confirm the group effect and refresh the resulting token/logon context.

findings.finding: WriteOwner/WriteDacl on the target object
findings.check: Preserve original state and validate each intermediate right.

fallback.reason: The right is not effective for the controlled principal: discard that edge and inspect another verified relationship.

lateral-movement.title: Test the destination from the real source
lateral-movement.note: A working password on one service does not establish execution permission on another host.

findings.finding: WinRM is reachable and the account has endpoint rights
findings.check: Use the WinRM procedure and verify the resulting token.

findings.finding: SMB/RPC is reachable and service-control rights are confirmed
findings.check: Use the service-execution procedure with a separate output path.

fallback.reason: Only the listener is reachable: inspect actual endpoint authorization before selecting an execution tool.

lateral-movement.title: Match password, hash, key or ticket to the client
lateral-movement.note: Use the existing Impacket/NetExec protocol-specific examples; do not treat successful authentication as remote execution.

findings.finding: Accepted authentication plus remote service rights
findings.check: Check share/SCM permissions and output reachability.

findings.finding: WMI/task rights with RPC/DCOM connectivity
findings.check: Check the exact namespace/task authorization and output channel.

fallback.reason: The artifact is rejected: recheck identity scope, material format, service name and transport.

pivoting.title: Enumerate what the pivot can actually reach
pivoting.note: Run route/listener checks on the pivot itself; do not infer its access from the attacker machine.

findings.finding: One internal TCP endpoint is reachable from the pivot
findings.check: Draw the local/pivot listener and initiator before choosing a fixed forward.

findings.finding: Several internal services need proxy/routed access
findings.check: Match the client protocol to SOCKS or a TUN route.

fallback.reason: The pivot cannot reach the destination: fix that leg before adding a tunnel.

pivoting.title: Use SSH forwarding for the required direction
pivoting.note: Use this when the attacker can SSH to a pivot that can reach the destination; remote forwarding reverses the listener placement.

findings.finding: The forwarded service responds through the listener
findings.check: Re-enumerate that destination with the matching service client.

findings.finding: Only the pivot can initiate the tunnel connection
findings.check: Select the reverse/listener arrangement deliberately.

fallback.reason: The listener exists but the app fails: test destination reachability and DNS through the chosen path.

pivoting.commands:
```bash
ssh -N \
  -L 127.0.0.1:LOCAL_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT \
  -p SSH_PORT USER@PIVOT \
  -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
  -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3
```

pivoting.title: Use Ligolo for a justified routed requirement
pivoting.note: Use the version-specific agent/proxy procedure and route setup. A tunnel session alone is not a working destination route.

findings.finding: The selected subnet is routed and the destination responds
findings.check: Re-run service discovery from that new position.

findings.finding: Delivery works but the payload callback fails
findings.check: Build and verify the separately needed return/callback path.

fallback.reason: Route/session setup fails: inspect the route, interface privileges and each connection leg.

execution.title: Find the first failed runtime boundary
execution.note: Check bytes, file type, architecture and runtime before trying another payload.

findings.finding: Wrong architecture or executable format
findings.check: Fix the artifact/build before re-running it.

findings.finding: The file reaches a different parser than expected
findings.check: Inspect quoting, encoding and the exact invocation.

fallback.reason: The artifact runs but no session appears: inspect handler and packet direction.

execution.commands:
```bash
file FILE
sha256sum FILE
readelf -l FILE 2>/dev/null
uname -m
```

execution.title: Match the payload handler and connection direction
execution.note: Keep the exact payload/session type, listener address and actual initiator together.

findings.finding: Handler settings match but no packet arrives
findings.check: Check the callback route from the target, including any pivot.

findings.finding: A session opens under the expected identity
findings.check: Verify the host and make the command channel usable.

fallback.reason: A connection immediately dies: inspect the actual process/session lifecycle rather than assuming a working shell.

integration.title: Capture the access transition while it is reproducible
integration.note: Keep commands/output, host and identity beside the transition that produced them.

findings.finding: A new identity, host or route
findings.check: Re-enumerate from that exact new position.

findings.finding: The final objective is evidenced
findings.check: Build the report from the reproducible chain.

fallback.reason: A transition lacks proof: repeat its specific verification before connecting it to another method.

integration.title: When stuck, return to the last working boundary
integration.note: Preserve the working session/route. Change one failed layer at a time.

findings.finding: Authentication works but an action is denied
findings.check: Inspect service/object authorization under that same identity.

findings.finding: A new credential or route has not been used for enumeration
findings.check: Update the host/identity/route state and revisit the accessible surface.

fallback.reason: Several guesses added no evidence: switch to a missing enumeration check, not a more exotic payload.

integration.commands:
```text
LAST WORKING STATE | FIRST FAILED BOUNDARY | EXACT ERROR | CHANGED CONDITION | DISCRIMINATING TEST
```
